Defines the legal boundary of the whole tender landscape for banking/payments buyers (state bodies, Banka Slovenije, public utilities).

candidates.source_name: PISRS – Zakon o dostopu do informacij javnega značaja (ZDIJZ)
candidates.why_relevant: The FOI statute. Articles 6.a/6.č/10.a define absolute public data on contracts of entities under dominant public-law influence and mandatory online publication — the legal hook for obtaining banking/payments contracts and annexes that never appear on the procurement portal.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Fetch consolidated text; extract article 6.a, 6.č, 10.a for a disclosure-rules cheat sheet
queries_used: Informacijski pooblaščenec odločba dostop do informacij javnega značaja pogodba banka

candidates.source_name: Informacijski pooblaščenec (IPRS) – Iskalnik po odločbah (FOI decisions search)
candidates.why_relevant: Searchable database of Information Commissioner appeal decisions. Decisions routinely name the applicant, the liable body and the concrete contract in dispute — including bank/financial-institution cases — and often reproduce contract details. The single richest route to contracts that were withheld and then ordered disclosed.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl the decisions index (per-decision pages use opaque hash slugs, e.g. /iskalnik-po-odlocbah/605093ff23262); keyword filter on 'banka', 'plačilni', 'pogodba', 'javno naročilo'

negative_findings.description: Searched for Inštitut Danes je nov dan's own procurement-research output. Found only company-registry and third-party references to its role in the Supervizor/Erar lineage; no current institute-hosted procurement study or dataset page was located in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Erar is now presented as a KPK-operated application (relaunched 5 March 2025); Danes je nov dan appears only indirectly.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell brief names this NGO as a research source; if it no longer maintains procurement tooling, later rounds should route to KPK/Erar and OPSI instead of the institute.

negative_findings.description: Slovenian-language academic search for procurement studies returned green-procurement theses and general transparency dissertations; nothing specific to banking/payments procurement in Slovenia.
negative_findings.result_summary: Repositories identified (CEK EF UL, DK FDV, UM), but no banking/payments procurement study surfaced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Academic literature is unlikely to be a productive lane for this cell; effort is better spent on IPRS decisions, DKOM and Court of Audit reports.

negative_findings.description: A guessed non-percent-encoded IPRS decisions-search path (https://www.ip-rs.si/informacije-javnega-znacaja/iskalnik-po-odlocbah) returned HTTP 404.
negative_findings.result_summary: The percent-encoded form from search results is recorded instead; treated as a path issue, not a dead source.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collectors must preserve Slovenian diacritics in IPRS URLs (č, š, ž percent-encoded) or every fetch will 404.

negative_findings.description: No single national register of signed public contract texts (as opposed to notices) was found for Slovenia.
negative_findings.result_summary: Contract texts appear only via ZDIJZ requests, IPRS decisions, Erar transactions, and case-by-case publication under ZDIJZ art. 10.a.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms that contract-level intelligence in SI is FOI-driven, not register-driven — a structural fact for the whole workstream.

coverage_gaps.description: Below-threshold 'evidenčna naročila' are not published as notices; only aggregate statistics and a >10,000 EUR annual listing duty exist. Many banking/payments purchases (software modules, terminal maintenance, card supplies) plausibly sit under the threshold.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Extract the current threshold values from the ZJN-3 NPB text and the latest MJU statistical report, then use Erar transaction data to see the sub-threshold layer.

coverage_gaps.description: The structure and rate limits of the enarocanje.si /arhiv/{id}/ archive and of the IPRS decisions index (opaque hash slugs) were not established in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a small deterministic probe of both to establish pagination, id ranges and robots.txt constraints before designing a collector.

coverage_gaps.description: No CPV code list for banking/payments/terminal procurement was assembled in this cell.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Compile the relevant CPV codes (financial services 66xxxxxx, IT 72xxxxxx, terminal/ATM hardware 30xxxxxx) so TED and e-JN queries can be scoped.

coverage_gaps.description: The separate regime for utilities/infrastructure buyers (ZJN-3 'infrastrukturno področje') and for the ZJNPOV defence/security act was noted only in passing.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Map which banking/payments-adjacent buyers fall under the infrastructure regime, since notice duties and thresholds differ there.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language coverage of Slovenian procurement rules is thin outside TED; national notices are published in Slovenian only.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Plan for machine translation of Slovenian notice and decision text rather than relying on English-language sources.

brief: Slovenia's procurement-disclosure landscape rests on two statutes, both fully readable on PISRS: ZJN-3 (what must be published, where, and above which thresholds) and ZDIJZ (what contract content can be extracted afterwards, including the absolute-public-data rules for entities under dominant public-law influence). Notices of record live on the Uradni list-operated Portal javnih naročil (enarocanje.si, with an /arhiv/ path for superseded notices) and, above EU thresholds, are duplicated to TED in eForms with English summaries — TED is the more tractable archive for structured collection. Contract texts themselves have no national register: they surface case-by-case through Informacijski pooblaščenec appeal decisions, DKOM review decisions, Court of Audit reports, and Erar's transaction-level spending data, which together also expose the sub-threshold 'evidenčna naročila' layer that notices hide. The main open risks for later rounds are the unknown crawlability of the enarocanje.si and IPRS indexes, the missing CPV scope list for banking/payments, and the fact that the NGO lane (Danes je nov dan) appears to have handed its tooling to state operators.
